newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean police raid Hanbo offices in loan probe.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean police raid Hanbo offices in loan probe.

text.p: South Korean police on Tuesday raided offices of the troubled Hanbo Group after allegations of misconduct in a loan scandal centred on the company's failed steel unit, state radio said.
The raid came one day after President Kim Young-sam ordered a thorough investigation into South Korea's 14th largest industrial conglomerate.

The Korea Broadcasting System said police were looking for loan-related documents at Hanbo Steel Co and the office of Hanbo founder Chung Tae-soo. State prosecutors were not immediately available for comment. Finance ministry officials say Hanbo borrowed about five trillion won ($5.8 billion) from banks and financial institutions, about 20 times its net worth.

Chung, banned from leaving the country along with several Hanbo executives, had paid into a slush fund raised by former president Roh Tae-woo, now serving a 17-year jail term for corruption and human rights abuses.

A criminal court trying Roh and Chung, along with other tycoons, found that the Hanbo chairman gave 15 billion won to Roh during his presidency but acquitted Chung, saying the payments were extracted under political pressure.

Opposition parties, calling the loans the biggest financial scandal in the country's history, say the loans to Hanbo Steel, the group's flagship, would not have been possible without government influence-peddling.
Hanbo Steel defaulted on debt last week and is seeking court protection with three other group units.

Officials of the ruling New Korea Party said its parliamentary leader was due to meet his opposition counterparts later on Tuesday to discuss reopening the National Assembly to discuss the Hanbo scandal.
The ruling party on Monday agreed to a separate parliamentary probe into Hanbo on condition it did not hamper the investigation by state prosecutors.

The main opposition National Congress for New Politics and United Liberal Democratic Party said they believed the government supported loans to Hanbo despite its shaky financial status. They said it was impossible for banks to provide such huge loans to Hanbo "without protection and influence-peddling at the heart of the power".
